sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know *aunque* from A2 Unit 28, and in the first lesson of this unit it took the subjunctive for a possibility. *Por más que* is a stronger version for effort or amount: "however much, no matter how much". It says that the action can go as far as you like and the result will not change. It takes the subjunctive, because the amount of effort is open and does not matter: *Por más que insistas, no voy a cambiar de idea*. *Por mucho que* works in the same way.

sections.title: However much, however...
rows: Por más que insistas, no voy a cambiar de idea.
However much you insist, I'm not going to change my mind.
Por mucho que cueste, lo vamos a hacer.
However much it costs, we're going to do it.
Por más que grites, nadie te va a oír.
No matter how much you shout, nobody will hear you.
Por muy difícil que sea, voy a intentarlo.
However difficult it is, I'm going to try. (*Por muy* + adjective + *que* + subjunctive.)
Por más que insistió, no consiguió nada.
No matter how much he insisted, he got nowhere. (It really happened: indicative.)

sections.title: How to build it
sections.content: Use *por más que* or *por mucho que* before a verb, and *por muy* + adjective or adverb + *que* before a quality: *por muy difícil que sea*. The main clause usually says that the result stays the same, so it often has *no* or *nadie* in it. When you tell a story and the effort really took place, you may also read the indicative (*Por más que insistió*), but when you look ahead or speak in general, use the subjunctive.

items.spanish: Por más que estudies, necesitas descansar.
items.english: No matter how much you study, you need to rest.

items.spanish: Por mucho que cueste, vamos a terminar el proyecto.
items.english: However much it costs, we're going to finish the project.

items.spanish: Por muy cansado que esté, siempre ayuda a su madre.
items.english: However tired he is, he always helps his mother.

items.spanish: Por más que lo intentó, no pudo abrir la puerta.
items.english: However hard he tried, he couldn't open the door.

sections.content: Compare the two: *aunque cueste* means "even if it costs" (the cost is one possibility), and *por mucho que cueste* means "however much it costs" (any amount at all). The second one stresses that the quantity makes no difference.
